newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: LatAm bourses seen reined in by U.S. rate worries.
newsitem.headline: LatAm bourses seen reined in by U.S. rate worries.

text.p: Latin American stock markets were seen stifled by recurring U.S. interest rate fears and domestic factors this week, shortened to four days by the May Day holiday Thursday.

Most bolsas braced for the raft of key U.S. economic indicators, to be issued this week starting Tuesday. The data is expected to transfix Wall Street, which is looking for insight as to what action the U.S. Federal Reserve will take on interest rates at a May 20 meeting of its policy-makers.

Brazilian stocks, however, were also seen hinging on court action on the privatization of the world's largest iron producer, while company results caused some anxiety in Chile and Mexico, and Venezuela looked aimless.
Brazil's government plans to auction off Tuesday a 40-45 percent stake in Cia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) VAL.Sa in the largest-ever privatization in Latin America.
An injunction granted Friday halting the selloff is likely to be overturned, but a host of other last-minute lawsuits are expected before the 1000 local/0900 EDT auction, brokers said.
"If there is no CVRD sale, people will sell. If the sale goes ahead, they won't sell," a trader in Sao Paulo said.

Wednesday's planned sale of a minority stake in state power distributor CEB was expected to give electricity shares a boost, but prices will also depend largely on this week's release of key U.S. indicators.
The bolsa's blue-chip Bovespa index rose 0.2 percent Friday to 9,732. It closed up 3.9 percent last week on hefty volume due to last Tuesday's options settlements.
Mexican stocks were seen hurt by Wall Street jitters and a cool reaction to first quarter earnings, analysts said.

"There are factors that worsen the bourse's response to volatility in the Dow Jones...But we see the IPC heading for support at 3,700 points," said Roberto Galvan, an analyst at the Bursametrica consultancy in Mexico City.
The leading IPC index shed 25.81 points or 0.7 percent last week to 3,762.62.
Many analysts expressed qualified disappointment at the crop of company earnings released recently.
"Reports have tended to come in a little below expectations in terms of sales and operating earnings...but they are not too bad as far as cash flow and margins are concerned," Galvan added.
Chilean blue chips were also seen angling lower in cautious trade, with investors focusing on first quarter results and U.S. indicators.
Company results may spark profit-taking because in many cases profits have been factored into prices and "won't justify the current level of the market," one dealer said.
"The market looks very mixed. The bias will depend very much on the United States," one dealer said.
But any fall would be gentle with blue chips seen continuing to hover in their trading range of 114-119 points.
The 40-share index ended virtually unchanged last week at 117.1 points.
Argentine stocks were seen almost exclusively focused on Wall Street.

"This looks like a difficult week," said Maximiliano Goff at traders Rio Research. "We lost the momentum that was provided last week by Standard & Poor's corporate credit risk upgrades and have fallen back into step with New York, so we recommend a lot of caution."
The blue-chip MerVal index gained 1.7 percent last week to 715.48, mainly driven Standard & Poor's decision to raise the rating of several local firms to investment-grade.
But volume dwindled to a puny 12.7 million pesos by the end of the week, denoting the hesitant tone of the market.
Venezuelan stocks were seen slightly more active but still lacking relevant news, dealers said.

"A lot depends on what happens on the labor front," Inversiones y Valores broker Hector Perez said, referring to a bill reforming the crumbling social security and severance pay systems under study in Congress.
Bellwether Electricidad de Caracas was expected to keep posting gains and lead the market higher on widely expected rate rises in the near future.
The bolsa's 19-share index ended flat last week at 6,320.07.
((-- Carmen Pignotti, Buenos Aires Newsroom 541 318-0657))
